name: sing
description: 노래 합성 DSP — 악보(음표+가사 음절)와 말한 목소리 wav 를 받아 음정·박자를 악보대로 재합성하고 반주를 얹어 노래 wav 를 만듭니다. 채팅 표면 = 발견 계단(run_module_action) 하나 — 노래는 vocal:true 선언이면 됩니다.

action.description: render = score -> song. Returns data.media with the wav url (put it in a `listening` component's audioUrl) and, with midiOut, the .mid beside it. scores = list the shelved scores (alias + filename) — check it FIRST when the user refers to an uploaded/shelved piece, then pass the alias as render's scoreMediaPath. You cannot recall a real melody from memory: an existing song plays from a MIDI (scoreMediaPath); a score you write yourself is a NEW composition and must be presented as one. selftest = self-checks, no files needed.

vocal.description: [render] true = SING it: the framework synthesizes a spoken TTS take and this module retunes it onto the melody's notes. The words come from the score's own lyrics, or from `lyrics` when the score has none. Needs a server TTS key; 64 syllables max — one verse. Omitted/false = instrumental. A melody written far outside a singable register is folded by whole octaves onto the take's own range, the way a singer transposes a song.

score.description: The song. {bpm, notes:[{syl, note, beats}], chords?:[{root, beats, quality?}], style?, band?, meter?, swing?, comp?, bassline?, drumPattern?} — note/root are pitch names like 'G4'/'C3'; beats are quarter-note counts; syl is the syllable sung on that note ('-' extends the previous one). style is a genre row (groove + feel + default band): trot | ballad | rock | metal | punk | pop | dance | rnb | hiphop | rocknroll | funk | jazz | blues | country | folk | carol | march | classic | strings | newage | none, plus aliases (edm, house, kpop, jpop, waltz, rap, swing, christmas, orchestra, symphony, 관현악, 오케스트라 = classic — full orchestra with winds, horns and dynamics-driven percussion; 현악/stringensemble = strings — string orchestra only) — an unknown style is refused with the full list.

band.description: Per-part instrument override {melody?, chord?, bass?} — any of the module's own patches (electric/acoustic guitar, e-violin, synth leads, piano, e-piano, organ, accordion, strings, brass, flute, marimba, bell, music box…) OR any General MIDI name (sax, cello, vibraphone, trumpet, harp, sitar, choir…): GM names sound native on the sf2 engine and borrow the nearest builtin timbre otherwise. A flat list works too — assigned to melody/chord/bass in order, drum words skipped (the kit comes from style/drumPattern). Unknown names are refused with the full library. Official GM spellings ('acoustic grand piano') are absorbed — case/spacing ignored. A "doubles" list inside band adds section doublings - the orchestral unison: [{"part": melody|chord|bass, "instrument", "octave": -2..2, "vel"?}] plays the same line on another instrument (flute an octave above, cello below). classic/orchestra and march carry a default set; an explicit list replaces it.

meter.description: Beats per bar: 4 (default), 3, or anything 2-12 — "5/4", "6/8", "7/8" spellings are absorbed (the numerator is read). 3 and 4 use each genre's hand-written groove; other meters derive theirs from the bar's grouping (5 = 3+2, 7 = 3+2+2, compound = threes): kick on group heads, backbeat on alternating groups.

swing.description: 0-1: how late the rhythm section's offbeat eighths lean (0 straight, 1 full shuffle). Omit for the style's default (trot swings lightly). The melody always stays straight.

comp.description: How the chord part moves: pad (held) | stabs (offbeat strokes) | arp (rippling eighths) | quarters. Omit for the style's default.

bassline.description: How the bass moves: hold (whole notes + pickup into the next chord) | twobeat (root-fifth alternation) | alt (marching quarters) | walk (quality-aware root-third-fifth quarters — the jazz/blues floor). Omit for the style's default.

drumPattern.description: Custom drum bar loop replacing the style's: rows of [drumName, beatInBar, velocity 0-1] looped every bar (fills and crashes still apply). Drum names = the full GM kit — kick, snare, rim, clap, hat/ohat, toms, ride, crash, china, splash, cowbell, tamb, congas, bongos, timbales, agogo, cabasa, maracas, guiro, claves, woodblocks, cuica, triangle… An unknown name is refused with the whole kit list.

bars.description: Bar count when the piece is longer than its notes/chords — with drumPattern and NO notes this makes a drum solo.

humanize.description: 0-1 human feel: deterministic micro timing/velocity jitter and chord rolls. '사람처럼' ≈ 0.5-0.7. Omit = exact grid.

pedal.description: Sustain pedal, three states: omit = play exactly what the score writes (marks become real CC64 automatically); true = ALSO pedal bar-by-bar when the score has no marks (월광 어법); false = dry — strip even the written marks.

voicing.description: 0-1 pianist's voicing: the top line sings out, inner voices step back, the bass supports quietly. '살랑살랑/은은하게/부드럽게' ≈ 0.6-0.8 (pairs well with humanize and pedal). Omit = the score's flat balance, which is what any GM player does — measured on Moonlight, the flat balance reads as gloom because the bass ends up loudest.

vocalPath.description: Workspace-relative path of the spoken vocal wav (the TTS output, one take of all lyrics in note order). Omitted = instrumental only.

scoreMediaPath.description: MIDI or MusicXML (전자악보 — .musicxml/.mxl/.xml, MuseScore's format) to use as the score when `score` is omitted — a media URL (/user/media/<slug>.mid), a workspace path, or the ALIAS of a shelved score. One procedure at any shelf size: check the `scores` action, pass the alias (matching ignores case/spacing and accepts the filename too). Re-instrument in the SAME call with top-level style/band/drumPattern — an existing piece never needs a composed score. Karaoke MIDIs and MusicXML bring their own lyrics (MusicXML plays its WHOLE notation: repeats/voltas/D.C./D.S. expand, tempo changes and metronome marks apply, 8va/transposing instruments sound right, wedges ramp dynamics, staccato/accents/graces/trills/fermatas/arpeggios and pedal marks all play); the parsed score comes back in data.score for correction.

lyricsMediaPath.description: [render, lyrics] Lyrics source for karaoke: a rhythm-lyric lead sheet (MusicXML whose lyrics ride slash/unpitched notes), a karaoke MIDI, or a ready-made .lrc file - media URL, workspace path, or shelf ALIAS (same matching as scoreMediaPath). Emits a synced .lrc beside the audio (data.lrcPath + media). Two-track karaoke = accompaniment score in scoreMediaPath + the lyric file here. A .lrc passes through with its own line spacing, re-stamped by lrcOffset.

lyricsQuery.description: [render, lyrics] Fetch synced lyrics from the internet (lrclib, the open successor of the old Winamp lyric plugins) by '가수 곡명', e.g. '조정석 아로하'. render attaches the find as the .lrc and reports the pick in data.lrcSource (a miss is a note, the audio still renders); the lyrics action just downloads and returns the path. Ignored when lyricsMediaPath is set.

durationSec.description: [lyrics] Target recording length in seconds — picks the right version when a song exists in several cuts.

lrc.description: [render] Emit an .lrc from the MAIN score's own lyrics (karaoke MIDI / vocal score with syllables). lyricsMediaPath implies this - set lrc only when the melody score itself carries the words.

lrcOffset.description: [render, lyrics] Shift every LRC timestamp by this many seconds (+0.5 = half a second later, negative = earlier, clamped at 0). Aligns lyrics to a recording whose intro length differs from the score.

lyrics.description: [render] Syllables to lay onto an existing score's notes, in order — works for ANY score passed as scoreMediaPath (MIDI or MusicXML), not just MIDI, and is used when that score carries no lyrics of its own. This is how you sing a shelved guide melody: pass the score's alias as scoreMediaPath, the words here, and vocal:true. Writing a new `score` by hand throws the guide melody away. Whitespace ignored; extra notes become melisma '-'.

style.description: Style (genre) override when the score comes from MIDI — any style name the score contract accepts; an unknown one is refused with the full list. ⚠️ scoreMediaPath 가 이미 편곡된 악보(밴드스코어 등)면 style 은 그 편곡을 우리가 만든 반주로 **교체**합니다 — 노래방 MR 처럼 원곡 그대로 연주하려면 style 을 주지 마세요. 사용자가 장르를 직접 말했을 때만 씁니다.

band.description: [render] Instrument override for the piece (works WITH scoreMediaPath — no need to compose a score to pick instruments): {melody?, chord?, bass?}, e.g. {"melody":"piano"}. Names = the module's own patches (piano, epiano, organ, accordion, aguitar/cguitar/eguitar/dguitar, eviolin, strings, brass, flute, marimba, bell, musicbox, synthlead, squarelead, synthbass, bass) or ANY General MIDI instrument — official spellings like 'acoustic grand piano' are absorbed, case/spacing ignored. A flat list is assigned to melody/chord/bass in order; drum words in it are skipped (drums come from style or drumPattern). Unknown names are refused with the full library. A "doubles" list inside band adds section doublings - the orchestral unison: [{"part": melody|chord|bass, "instrument", "octave": -2..2, "vel"?}] plays the same line on another instrument (flute an octave above, cello below). classic/orchestra and march carry a default set; an explicit list replaces it.

drumPattern.description: [render] Custom drum bar loop (works WITH scoreMediaPath): rows of [drumName, beatInBar, velocity 0-1], looped every bar — e.g. [["kick",0,0.9],["snare",1],["snare",3]]. A {"kick":[0,2],"snare":1} map also reads. Drum names = the full GM kit (kick, snare, rim, clap, hat, ohat, toms, ride, crash, china, splash, cowbell, tamb, congas, bongos, timbales, agogo, cabasa, maracas, guiro, claves, woodblocks, cuica, triangle...); an unknown name is refused with the whole list. Omit to keep the style's own groove — style fills stay either way.

swing.description: 0-1: how late the rhythm section's offbeat eighths lean (0 straight, 1 full shuffle). Omit for the style's default (trot swings lightly). The melody always stays straight.

comp.description: How the chord part moves: pad (held) | stabs (offbeat strokes) | arp (rippling eighths) | quarters. Omit for the style's default.

bassline.description: How the bass moves: hold (whole notes + pickup into the next chord) | twobeat (root-fifth alternation) | alt (marching quarters) | walk (quality-aware root-third-fifth quarters — the jazz/blues floor). Omit for the style's default.

engine.description: [render] sf2 = system FluidSynth + GM SoundFont — realistic instruments; the server enables it with `apt install fluidsynth fluid-soundfont-gm` and the module finds both on its own. builtin = the module's own synth. Omit = auto: sf2 when installed, else builtin.

audioFormat.description: [render] Container for the rendered audio. **Omit it.** flac is the default and is the right answer unless the person asked for something else in words: lossless, plays everywhere, and twenty times cheaper to encode on a small server (measured on a 4-minute render: flac 24MB in 0.4s, wav 47MB, mp3 4.6MB in 8.3s, opus 3.7MB in 7.9s). Set it only to carry a request that was actually made — "작게"/"용량" for mp3 or opus, "편집용 원본" for wav. Length alone is not a reason to change it.

bpm.description: [render, with scoreMediaPath] Override the file's tempo (quarter-note BPM, 20-300). '템포 빠르게' = a higher number.

humanize.description: 0-1 human feel: deterministic micro timing/velocity jitter and chord rolls. '사람처럼' ≈ 0.5-0.7. Omit = exact grid.

voicing.description: [render, with scoreMediaPath] 0-1 pianist's voicing: the top line sings out, inner voices step back, the bass supports quietly. '살랑살랑/은은하게/부드럽게' ≈ 0.6-0.8 (pairs well with humanize and pedal). Omit = the score's own balance, which is what any GM player does and the default here.

pedal.description: [render, with scoreMediaPath] Sustain pedal, three states: omit = play exactly what the score writes (marks become real CC64 automatically); true = ALSO pedal bar-by-bar when the score has no marks (월광 어법); false = dry — strip even the written marks.

outPath.description: Workspace-relative output wav path. Default data/sing/out-<hash>.wav

midiOut.description: Also write the arrangement as a .mid beside the wav (data.media then carries both, and the chat shows a download card). Only set this when the user asks for the MIDI file — the wav alone is the normal answer.

midiOutPath.description: Workspace-relative .mid path. Implies midiOut. Default = the wav path with a .mid extension.

query.description: [scores] Filter the shelf by substring of alias or filename (case/spacing ignored). Omit for the whole shelf.

path.description: [preview] The score file to hear: a media path, a URL, or a shelf alias.

voice.description: [render] Which TTS voice sings, by the server provider's own voice name. Omit to use the voice configured in settings. Set it only to carry a request that was made in words ("여자 목소리로", "낮은 남자 목소리로") — the singer is not the model's choice. Choosing a voice that fits the song's register is the real fix for a melody that sits too high or too low; the octave fold is only the safety net under it.

actionCatalog.name: 곡 렌더 (악보 → 노래·연주)
actionCatalog.description: score 또는 scoreMediaPath 를 wav 로 렌더합니다 — 노래(vocal:true)·연주곡·장르 반주. data.media 가 재생 URL 을 돌려줍니다. 노래방 = 반주 악보(scoreMediaPath)로 MR 을, 가사 악보나 .lrc(lyricsMediaPath)로 싱크 가사 .lrc 를 한 콜에 만듭니다. 가사는 lyricsQuery('가수 곡명')로 인터넷(lrclib)에서 자동으로 찾아 붙일 수도 있습니다. 취향 노브(style·humanize·voicing·pedal·swing·comp·bassline·drumPattern) = **사용자가 그 표현을 말했을 때 그 말을 옮기는 칸**입니다('사람처럼'→humanize, '락으로'→style). 그런 말이 없는 요청의 답은 악보와 미디 기본값 그대로입니다.

actionCatalog.name: 악보 미리듣기 (MIDI → 소리)
actionCatalog.description: 악보 파일(path) 하나를 있는 그대로 소리로 구워 재생 URL 을 돌려줍니다 — 브라우저는 MIDI 를 재생하지 못하므로 이쪽에서 만듭니다. 같은 파일은 한 번만 굽고 이후에는 그 결과를 찾아 돌려줍니다. 작곡·편곡·취향 노브 없음(악보 그대로), 가사 없음.

actionCatalog.name: 악보 보관함 조회
actionCatalog.description: 보관함의 악보 목록·검색 (별칭·파일명) — render 전에 이걸 먼저 거칩니다. 기존 곡이면 별칭을 scoreMediaPath 로 넘기고 악기·스타일은 같은 호출의 band/style 로 함께 지정합니다(재작곡 불필요). 없으면 새로 작곡합니다.

actionCatalog.name: 가사 검색·싱크 조정 (인터넷 LRC)
actionCatalog.description: 곡명·가수(lyricsQuery)로 lrclib 에서 싱크 가사(.lrc)를 내려받거나, 기존 가사 파일(lyricsMediaPath)을 lrcOffset 으로 전체 밀고 당겨 다시 찍습니다 — 오디오 재렌더 없이 가사만. 반환 path 를 render 의 lyricsMediaPath 로 쓰면 됩니다.

actionCatalog.name: 셀프테스트
actionCatalog.description: Offline checks over the synth, arrangement and shelf logic. No files, no network.
